Class ManagerPanel

java.lang.Object
java.awt.Component
java.awt.Container
javax.swing.JComponent
javax.swing.JPanel
GUI.ManagerPanel
All Implemented Interfaces:
ImageObserver, MenuContainer, Serializable, Accessible
public class ManagerPanel extends JPanel
Manager screen: tabs for viewing and editing the menu, inventory, employees and toppings, plus read-only reports (popular drinks, recent orders, an hourly order graph and the X-report).
Author:
calebxu, Cody Cheng, Hayden Futch

    • populateTableContainer

      private void populateTableContainer(JPanel container, PreparedStatement pstmt) throws SQLException
      Runs a report query and adds its results to the container as a read-only, sortable table. Column headers are taken from the query's column names, so aliases in the SELECT become the headers the manager sees.
      Parameters:
      container - the panel to add the scrollable table to
      pstmt - the prepared query, with all parameters already set
      Throws:
      SQLException - if the query fails; the caller shows the error

      private void setDrinkActive(boolean makeActive, JPanel tableContainer)

    • showIngredientsDialog

      private void showIngredientsDialog(int menuItemId, String drinkName)
      Opens a pop-up listing a drink's current ingredients from menu_item_ingredients, with controls to add an ingredient (or change the amount of one already in the recipe) and to remove the selected one. Amounts are for a Small; the cashier screen uses x2 for Medium and x3 for Large.
      Parameters:
      menuItemId - the drink's menu_item_id
      drinkName - the drink's name, shown in the title

    • runRecipeUpdate

      private boolean runRecipeUpdate(Component parent, String sql, Object... params)
      Runs one INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on menu_item_ingredients for the pop-up. Unlike executeUpdate, it only speaks up on errors, so adding several ingredients isn't interrupted by a success dialog each time.
      Parameters:
      parent - the component to show errors over
      sql - the statement, with ? placeholders
      params - values bound to the placeholders, in order
      Returns:
      true if the statement ran without an error

    • addIngredientToBothTables

      private boolean addIngredientToBothTables(int id, String name, String units, double qty)
      Adds a new ingredient to both the inventory table (stock on hand) and the ingredients table (what drink recipes can reference), in one transaction so either both rows are saved or neither is. If the ingredients table already has a row with this ID, that row is kept as-is and only the inventory row is added. Shows a success or error dialog rather than throwing.
      Parameters:
      id - the ingredient_id, shared by both tables
      name - the ingredient name
      units - the units, e.g. oz or grams
      qty - the starting stock quantity
      Returns:
      true if the inventory row was added

      private void loadPopularDrinksData(JPanel container, String startDate, String timeframe)
